newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Senate panel caps FY98 EEP at $150 mln.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Senate panel caps FY98 EEP at $150 mln.

text.p: A Senate panel on Tuesday voted to cap funding for the United States' main agricultural export subsidy program at $150 million in fiscal 1998, well below the Clinton administration request of $500 million.

The Senate Appropriations subcommittee on agriculture approved the spending cap on the Export Enhancement Program as part of a fiscal 1998 spending bill for the U.S. Agriculture Department and the Food and Drug Administration.
Last week the House Appropriations Committee approved $205 million for EEP, which is being squeezed this year by lawmakers' desires to fund programs such as crop insurance.

The U.S. Department of Agriculture has not subsidized wheat and most other eligible commodities under EEP for almost two years. But with lower crop prices this year because of expected large harvests, there has been some speculation that USDA might revive the program.
In addition, Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said last week that the Clinton administration was looking at subsidizing wheat flour and barley malt exports to help win back lost market share.
Congress initially funded EEP at $100 million in fiscal 1997 but cut that to $10 million earlier this summer to help provide assistance for flood victims in the Northern Plains.
